domain: environmental regulation - federal impact-assessment lifecycle outcome (Canadian Impact Assessment Registry)
prediction_question: For a project assessment posted to the Canadian Impact Assessment Registry, at its registry start date, will the assessment process terminate before any determination or decision is issued (proponent withdrawal / process termination), rather than run to a determination?
prediction_time: The assessment's registry start date (published per project on the registry page and in the MapServer layer as start_date). Features available at that instant: the inventory attributes published with the posting (project category, province, responsible authority(ies), location type, coordinates, description text, start date). The terminal state and its dated event (Latest update line: termination date, or Notice-of-Determination date + outcome wording) and the layer's current project_state_en/updated_at are post-hoc label sources and never ship as features. The registry is a live current archive: no historical vintages of pages are published, so the task is retrospective-within-current-archive, anchored on the dated events the current pages preserve; it cannot claim historical operational availability.
target_definition: Binary: the assessment's terminal state is 'Terminated' (MapServer layer 2 membership; registry page 'Assessment status: Terminated' plus a dated termination line in 'Latest update', e.g. proj 81027 'January 18, 2022 - The assessment process has been terminated') vs 'Completed' with a dated determination (e.g. proj 84411 'August 29, 2023 - ... determined that the project is not likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects'). Label source columns: project_state_en, the page Latest-update text/date and Assessment status - all excluded from shipped features. Assessments still 'In progress' at fetch time are censored and must be handled by an explicit censoring rule, not dropped silently.

split_strategy: Temporal by registry start year. Volume era measured 2019+ (the IAA came into force 2019-08; pre-2019 rows in the layer are sparse backfill: 2006-2018 totals about 200 rows across 13 years). Measured starts/terminal counts per start year (state at 2026-10-30): 2019 215/16, 2020 836/48, 2021 968/51, 2022 907/47, 2023 956/48, 2024 917/32, 2025 944/29, 2026 650/7 (in-progress shares 5%, 8.5%, 9.4%, 12.2%, 15.7%, 17.6%, 22.0%, 55.1% - recent cohorts heavily right-censored). Candidate windows train 2019-2022 (2,926 starts / 162 terminal, 5.5%), eval 2023-2024 (1,873 / 80, 4.3%), holdout 2025-2026 (1,594 / 36, 2.3% BUT censored) - a holdout this recent needs an explicit censoring rule (e.g. fixed horizon from start date with unresolved rows excluded by rule, or push the holdout back once terminal-event lag is measured); pre-2019 rows usable only as documented partial backfill. Both classes present every year 2019-2026.

measurements.mapserver_probe_2026_10_30: Service info + per-layer counts + 8-record samples per layer (fields listed in sources). Total 6,600 projects: Completed 5,079, In progress 1,173, Terminated 348 (5.3%).
measurements.full_layer_fetch_2026_10_30: All 6,600 attribute rows (project_id, project_cat_en, province_codes, start_date, project_state_en; no geometry): 9 requests, 1,010,024 bytes, 6.58 s wall clock on the coordinator container. Retained probe script probe/iaac_layer_probe.py.
measurements.registry_page_samples_2026_10_30: 4 pages via extraction backend: 81027 Terminated (dated termination line 2022-01-18; non-designated project on federal lands), 84411 Completed (dated determination 2023-08-29, outcome wording 'not likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects'; clean text 149.8 KB mostly 'nearby assessments' nav noise), 80175 Completed designated CEAA-2012 project (key-documents table: Notice of Commencement 2019-07-05, EA Decision Statement 2021-01-11; 8.6 KB), 87425 In progress (dated latest update 2024-04-17, key-documents table with dates; 12.2 KB). Dated terminal events verified for 3/3 terminal-or-completed samples; sample size too small to generalize - the share of pages with parseable dated terminal events across the full cohort is the named next measurement.
measurements.novelty_search_preliminary_2026_10_30: Web search (queries: 'machine learning predicting environmental impact assessment outcome Canada decisions dataset', plus browsing of top results): no ML-ready benchmark or dataset found for predicting Canadian Impact Assessment Registry outcomes; results were CO2-emissions/LCA ML noise plus one Tandfonline review of AI-in-EIA literature (no registry-outcome task). A 2024 review of AI in EIA surfaced no outcome-prediction benchmark. Formal check-novelty.py with recorded verdict deferred until the bounded page-sample resolves extraction feasibility (investigating status).
measurements.registry_page_stratified_sample_2026_11_: 60-page stratified sample (24 Terminated + 24 Completed + 12 In progress, spread over start-years 2010-2026 with a 2019+ bias; seed 20261105; direct urllib fetches from the coordinator, 0 errors): (a) DATED machine-parseable terminal/most-recent event line in the page's 'Latest update' div, after entity normalization (  – — appear inside dates and separators; one line uses 'March 10 2026' comma-less): Terminated 20/24 (83%; 2019+ subsample 11/14), Completed 23/24 (96%; 2019+ 13/14), In progress 11/12 (92%). 3/24 Terminated pages carry terminal wording with NO parsable date ('The permit holder will not be proceeding with this project.', 'The project, as proposed, has been cancelled .', 'The environmental assessment process has been terminated.') - a named fallback class for construction: the page meta 'Modified Date' exists (e.g. 2024-12-11) but is last-edit, not event date, so these rows are either event-date-missing or resolved from the page's key-documents table; the rule is fixed before scoring. (b) Per-page cost measured: mean 170,415 B, mean 3.00 s -> 6,600 pages ESTIMATES to ~1.12 GB and ~5.5 h serial (bounded-concurrency worker job; estimate from the 60-page mean, labeled as such). (c) Outcome wording among Completed: 'determined that the project is not likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects' 11/24; 'likely to cause' 0/24 (expected-rare CONFIRMED at sample scale); 14/24 carry determination wording of any form. (d) Bulk export: NONE found - the registry listing page (iaac-aeic.gc.ca/050/evaluations, 30,981 B fetched 2026-11-05) has no export/CSV/RSS/bulk markers; per-page extraction is the only channel for dated events. CROSS-CHECK: page meta 'Status' == MapServer project_state_en on 60/60. NEW timing measurement: start_date -> dated-event lag on the 20 dated Terminated pages: min 0, p25 224, median 575, p75 1,583, max 3,917 days (long-tailed; the latest-update date is a proxy for the termination event where the line IS the terminal event - noisy for a few pages whose latest update is post-termination); censoring rule and holdout boundary need the cohort-scale distribution. Retained scripts: probe/iaac_page_sample.py (fetch + first-pass parse) and probe/iaac_reanalyze.py (entity-normalized final numbers); raw per-page results iaac_pages_sample.json kept in the session scratch, not the repo.
measurements.cost_unknown_page_extraction: RESOLVED 2026-11-05 by the 60-page stratified sample: mean 170,415 B and 3.00 s per page; 6,600-page cohort extraction ~= 1.12 GB, ~5.5 h serial - a bounded-concurrency worker prerequisite (see registry_page_stratified_sample_2026_11_05).

next_action: Cohort-scale dated-event extraction is the remaining worker prerequisite (advancement owns it), then ready/drop on measured criteria. Job: with bounded concurrency, fetch all 6,600 registry pages (~1.12 GB, ~5.5 h serial estimate), sha256-pin the harvest, parse the dated Latest-update lines with the entity-normalized grammar already measured ( /–/— inside dates, comma-less forms), and compute: (a) the FULL dated-terminal-event share per state and start-year (sample: Terminated 83%, Completed 96%), (b) the cohort-scale start->event lag distribution for BOTH terminal states (sample Terminated n=20: median 575 d, max 3,917 d) to fix the censoring rule and holdout boundary - a fixed-horizon censoring or a pushed-back holdout window, decided from the measured distribution, (c) the fate of the no-parsable-date terminal pages (sample 3/24 Terminated): event-date-missing class vs key-documents-table recovery, rule fixed before scoring, (d) per-window label counts for train 2019-2022 / eval 2023-2024 / holdout per the fixed censoring rule, with clustered counts. NOVELTY: the formal check is RECORDED (2026-11-05, verdict differentiated - see novelty_check; searches found only LCA-method ML papers, no registry-outcome task for any jurisdiction). ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA to flip ready: dated-event share >=80% in every state x era cell used, every window carries both classes with the censoring rule stated, and the lag distribution supports a holdout whose labels are observable by the archive end. FAILURE MODES to record instead: dated-event share below the threshold (timing contract unsupported - park with the measured share), or a censoring rule that leaves any window single-classed. NO construction was started; nothing here is scored or quotable as a base rate beyond the recorded sample.
verdict: investigating - extraction feasibility RESOLVED at sample scale (dated terminal-event lines 83-96%, per-page 170 KB / 3.0 s, no bulk export, novelty differentiated); the remaining gate to ready is the cohort-scale dated-event extraction + lag distribution (worker prerequisite)

novelty_check.theirs: The publisher (IAAC) ships the registry itself and an inventory MapServer (attributes without dated terminal events); no bulk export of dated events exists (measured 2026-11-05). Searches for outcome-prediction datasets return only life-cycle-assessment (LCA) methodology ML papers (Springer, ICAR, PMC demolition-tool SD+RF study, synthetic-data net-effects regression) - none predicts regulatory assessment outcomes, none covers any impact-assessment registry, no jurisdiction. The 2026-10-30 preliminary search (Canadian IA outcome prediction) found the same negative; a 2024 review of AI-in-EIA surfaced no registry-outcome task.
novelty_check.ours: First ML-ready prediction task on the Canadian Impact Assessment Registry lifecycle: at an assessment's registry start date, predict early termination (proponent withdrawal / process termination) vs running to a determination, over the full 6,600-project national cohort (2019+ IAA-era volume measured: ~650-970 starts/year, terminations every year 2019-2026), with per-project dated terminal events extracted from registry pages, temporal splits by start year, and an explicit censoring rule for in-progress cohorts.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
